Every fish in this sheet is a GOLDFISH (Carassius auratus): exactly one goldfish per cell, never a different species, never two fish. Use the goldfish varieties listed (fancy fantail, oranda, ryukyu, ranchu, black moor, or common/comet goldfish with koi-like red-and-white sarasa colors). Each goldfish is underwater in a home aquarium.
Row 1 column 1: orange-and-white fantail goldfish covered with many separate small WHITE salt-grain dots on body and fins (ich), each dot a distinct grain like sprinkled table salt.
Row 1 column 2: white-and-red oranda goldfish with a very fine GOLD-RUST powdery dust over the white parts of its back and fins (velvet), much finer than salt grains, like gold powder seen in side light; fins slightly clamped.
Row 1 column 3: black moor goldfish (normal eyes for a moor) with one localized fluffy WHITE COTTON-WOOL tuft of fine threads sticking out from a small wound on its flank (fungus / water mold).
Row 1 column 4: red common goldfish with a flat irregular PALE GREY-WHITE patch across its back just in front of the dorsal fin, like a saddle (columnaris); flat, no fluffy threads.
Row 2 column 1: calico fantail goldfish with RAGGED, SHORTENED, ROTTING tail and fin edges, uneven melted-looking edges with red-streaked margins (fin rot).
Row 2 column 2: red-and-white sarasa comet goldfish with one round OPEN RED SORE on its flank where scales are missing, a red crater with a white rim (goldfish ulcer).
Row 2 column 3: orange ryukyu goldfish with a very round SWOLLEN BELLY, scales still lying flat and smooth (bloat).
Row 2 column 4: close side view of an orange common goldfish head (not a telescope-eye) with one eye clearly BULGING OUT like a marble, slightly cloudy (popeye / eye problem).
Row 3 column 1: red-and-white oranda goldfish with rough white-pink CAULIFLOWER-LIKE wart clusters on the edge of its tail fin (raised lumps).
Row 3 column 2: orange comet goldfish at the very top of the water, mouth breaking the surface GASPING for air, gill covers flared, a few bubbles; the water surface line visible across the top of the cell.
Row 3 column 3: orange fantail goldfish FLOATING UPSIDE DOWN near the surface, belly up, unable to turn the right way (swim bladder problem). Water surface visible.
Row 3 column 4: dull, faded orange goldfish resting listlessly on the gravel bottom with FINS CLAMPED tightly against its body, no spots or wounds; looks fine but clearly not active.

review.method: Every sheet and every crop opened and checked for the right fish, the right sign visible, no text artifacts. A labelled contact image of all 120 crops was reviewed (workspace/.openclaw/tmp/fhl-fresh/all-crops.jpg).
repairs: fresh-fixes (repair sheet 1): all five extras sheets drew the 'injury' cell with an intact tail; velvet dust was nearly invisible on the livebearer (silver molly) and cichlid (ram). Repair sheet 1 fixed the dust (livebearer-dust, cichlid-dust used) but still drew intact tails.
fresh-injury (repair sheet 2): injury re-described as a chunk/notch missing from the tail; used for all five *-injury cells.

weakCells.goldfish-dust: gold dust is faint (velvet is subtle by nature; caption says to shine a torch).
weakCells.community-eyes: close-up of the neon is oddly framed, but the bulging eye is clear.
weakCells.community-flukes: neon tilted awkwardly against the rock; reads as rubbing.
weakCells.cichlid-dust: German blue ram is naturally yellowish, so the dust reads as speckled gold rather than a coating.
weakCells.cichlid-breathing: discus mouth looks exaggerated, but gasping at the surface is clear.
weakCells.catfish-injury: notches in the cory tail are visible but small at thumbnail size.
weakCells.catfish-on-side: panda cory reads as lying belly-up on the sand rather than on its side; still clearly a balance problem.

review.noPictureByDesign: goldfish, community, livebearer and catfish have no hole-in-the-head picture (a cichlid problem); those results fall back to the generic picture.
